gui_decision: Segment 0: choose bundled study profile or custom design
toolkit_control: Profile selector plus Custom design option; creates/activates registry folders and records profile metadata
study_examples: Published-profile recreation and software-methods workflows
design_rationale: Keeps a PPS task from becoming an undocumented local script; profile identity, verification status, and missing-parameter notes are part of the method
caveat: A verified profile means the represented fields were checked; it does not certify original-author stimulus equivalence

toolkit_control: Project name, profile id, source profile id, and local registry manifest
study_examples: Reusable experiment-builder precedents and open-toolbox papers
design_rationale: Human-readable naming supports audit, sharing, and later profile snapshots
caveat: Local custom profiles stay ignored until intentionally exported or packaged

toolkit_control: Profile citation metadata, DOI/source URL, verification status, and citation export where available
study_examples: Literature recreation profiles with partial/verified statuses
design_rationale: Makes paper-to-GUI translation visible before a lab treats a template as a replication
caveat: Some profile citations are source-pointer records and require manual paper review before exact replication claims

gui_decision: Segment 1: generate looming noise or import source
toolkit_control: Generated source bake plus custom looming/audio clip imports
study_examples: Dynamic sounds, rough sounds, speech/instruction clips, emotional/ecological sounds
design_rationale: Audio-tactile PPS designs vary by source identity and salience; the toolkit separates source creation from later trial scheduling
caveat: Imported third-party sounds are local assets unless redistribution rights are verified

gui_decision: Segment 1: source mode burst train versus smooth linear
toolkit_control: Two generated-noise modes: dynaspace_gaussian_burst_train and continuous_noise labeled Burst train and Smooth linear
study_examples: DynaSpace/mobile burst trains and older continuous/noise-like looming tasks
design_rationale: Burst trains preserve salient onset structure used by recent mobile/DynaSpace-style protocols; smooth linear remains available for older or explicit continuous designs
caveat: Mode choice is not a control condition by itself; papers must report waveform, burst duration, onset spacing, and envelope

gui_decision: Segment 1: loudness contract and gain law
toolkit_control: Start/end SPL policy, instruction offset, peak ceiling, renderer gain mode, and estimated-versus-measured calibration status
study_examples: Auditory distance perception and virtual nearby-source judgments depend on level, direct-to-reverberant ratio, source spectrum, source type, and normalization choices
design_rationale: Distance-at-touch can be confounded with loudness unless the gain law and calibration evidence are explicit
caveat: Estimated hardware SPL is not publication-grade acoustic calibration; final studies need measured participant-ear SPL or a stated limitation

gui_decision: Segment 1: choose noise or sound class
toolkit_control: White, pink, and other generated noise labels plus imported emotional/ecological/custom sounds
study_examples: White-noise dynamic sounds, rough harmonic sounds, dog/sheep rear sounds, affective looming sounds
design_rationale: Spectral content can alter salience, threat value, localization, and response readiness; labels and hashes make it reconstructable
caveat: Toolkit-generated proxies are not equivalent to proprietary or unredistributed original stimuli

toolkit_control: Trajectory radius/distance controls and trajectory inventory
study_examples: Canzoneri dynamic distances, Hobeika logarithmic distance sampling, smartphone DynaSpace anchors
design_rationale: Distance at tactile onset is often the theoretical PPS variable; storing sampled trajectory coordinates prevents later ambiguity
caveat: Virtual distance depends on renderer, HRTF choice, level law, and participant perceptual externalization

gui_decision: Segment 1: azimuth, elevation, and spatial direction
toolkit_control: Front/rear/left/right, azimuth, elevation, 2D/3D trajectory preview, source-level trajectory snapshots
study_examples: Four-direction, front/rear, left/right, VR/3D boundary, walking/remapping studies
design_rationale: PPS is body-relative and direction-sensitive; trajectory metadata must state where the sound approaches from, not only when the tactile event occurs
caveat: The current GUI can represent many audio-tactile trajectories but not every social, VR, locomotor, or apparatus-specific manipulation

toolkit_control: Looming/receding labels, path length, movement duration, and speed metadata
study_examples: Approaching versus receding dynamic-sound designs and motor/walking variants
design_rationale: Approach direction can change PPS facilitation and defensive relevance; speed determines the mapping from SOA to distance
caveat: Exact analog speaker or Unity motion implementations may require profile notes beyond the current binaural trajectory abstraction

toolkit_control: FABIAN/SOFA reference path, 3DTI-compatible config, render manifest, trajectory/QC CSVs
study_examples: Near-field HRTF datasets, 3D Tune-In real-time binaural spatialization, and near-field perceptual validation studies
design_rationale: Near-body PPS tasks depend on distance, ITD, ILD, level, near-field cues, and participant perceptual context; renderer version and SOFA metadata are part of the method
caveat: Generic FABIAN rendering is standardized but not individualized HRTF measurement; do not overclaim absolute perceived distance, externalization, or front/back localization

toolkit_control: OpenSesame-style row builder with row labels and folder-per-family outputs
study_examples: Inhale/exhale Study 5 rows; direction or condition families in published profiles
design_rationale: Row identity preserves repeated within-trial structure before randomization; later blocks should not erase the family scaffold
caveat: Some published protocols include training, social context, or motor states that remain profile metadata unless they change audio-tactile timing

toolkit_control: Left-to-right sequence of instruction snippets, jitter, and looming/source boxes
study_examples: Breathing/instruction plus looming tasks and run-level instruction workflows
design_rationale: Within-trial order affects expectancy and response preparation; visible boxes make temporal composition auditable
caveat: Instruction audio is local/imported and may not be part of original published protocols

toolkit_control: Multiple source labels in a box multiply concrete sequence variants
study_examples: Noise/color, direction, valence, and condition alternatives across PPS paradigms
design_rationale: Alternatives separate experimental factors from ad hoc file duplication and keep source balancing explicit
caveat: Crossed alternatives can exceed the GUI's representation if a paper also requires body-part or apparatus factors not yet modeled

toolkit_control: Timed silent intervals stored in sequence manifests
study_examples: ITI and onset jitter vary across reaction-time paradigms
design_rationale: Jitter controls temporal expectation and prevents fixed timing from becoming a hidden confound
caveat: The toolkit stores jitter values but exact ITI policies for some published profiles still require source extraction

toolkit_control: Speaker/play preview for resolved Segment 1 ingredients
study_examples: Stimulus-preview practices in experiment-builder software
design_rationale: Researchers need to inspect the exact source referenced by a row before baking downstream trials
caveat: Preview playback is a comfort/content check, not calibrated timing or SPL evidence

toolkit_control: Main SOA list and effective baseline SOA set
study_examples: Canzoneri T1-T5, Hobeika logarithmic sampling, DynaSpace anchors
design_rationale: SOA is the operational bridge from time to sound-source distance; manuscripts must report both timing and spatial interpretation
caveat: If distance at tactile onset is inferred from renderer metadata, the inference must be declared

toolkit_control: No baseline, tactile-only, min/max anchor, min+max, full-SOA tactile-only, stationary/fixed-distance auditory baseline, custom baselines
study_examples: Hobeika fixed-distance baseline, Teraoka tactile-only baseline, Canzoneri T0/T6 controls, Holmes critique
design_rationale: Baseline logic differs sharply across the field; exposing it prevents hidden subtraction choices and expectancy corrections
caveat: No single baseline is universally correct; papers must justify the baseline relative to their source trajectory and expectancy model

toolkit_control: Baseline stationary-burst leaf folders with tactile channel retained
study_examples: Study 5 local profiles and fixed-distance/static-sound controls
design_rationale: Stationary controls can separate looming dynamics from audio presence and tactile timing
caveat: Stationary-burst files are controls for the toolkit's chosen source standard, not proof that all expectancy effects are removed

toolkit_control: Auditory channels silenced or non-looming components preserved while tactile cue remains on channel 3
study_examples: Teraoka tactile-only baseline and Canzoneri pre/post tactile controls
design_rationale: Tactile-only baselines estimate unimodal tactile RT and allow baseline-corrected facilitation
caveat: Frequent tactile-only trials can alter target probability and miss rates; response probability must be tracked

toolkit_control: Catch-trial-ready stereo/binaural files without tactile cue
study_examples: Auditory-only catch trials in dynamic PPS studies
design_rationale: Catch trials quantify response bias and premature/false tactile reports
caveat: Catch rates must be reported because response probability can influence near-far benefits

gui_decision: Segment 3: tactile cue and channel map
toolkit_control: Shared tactile cue inserted in channel 3; channels 1-2 carry binaural audio
study_examples: Audio-tactile reaction-time and vibrotactile detection paradigms
design_rationale: Channel-role manifests prevent left/right/tactile ambiguity across renderer, runner, loopback, and analysis layers
caveat: Digital channel evidence is not equivalent to mechanical vibration onset or perceived tactile onset

toolkit_control: Global, folder-level, and per-WAV repetition controls; live trial-count and duration feedback
study_examples: PPS studies differ in trials per SOA, catch proportion, and condition balance
design_rationale: Repetition pools make response probability, cell counts, and duration visible before randomization
caveat: Fractional or adjusted repetitions should be documented as design decisions, not post-hoc balancing

toolkit_control: Estimated playback duration, average trial duration, and longest-folder contribution
study_examples: Long RT tasks and fatigue-sensitive tactile calibration workflows
design_rationale: Duration predicts fatigue, habituation, and operational burden; it belongs beside repetition choices
caveat: Duration estimates exclude operator delays and participant breaks unless those are encoded

toolkit_control: Seeded distribution from repetition pool into block CSVs
study_examples: Reproducible randomization in experiment-builder systems and constrained-sequence tools
design_rationale: Block CSVs are methods artifacts; they let labs inspect actual row order before running participants
caveat: Randomization constraints do not replace counterbalancing or preregistered analysis plans

toolkit_control: Hard row-order scaffold with Gellermann-style within-family queues
study_examples: Study 5 inhale/exhale alternation, balanced family designs, and constrained randomization examples
design_rationale: Preserves within-trial family rhythm while still distributing concrete conditions and making sequential constraints auditable
caveat: Some published studies may require fully randomized rows; over-constrained sequences can add their own structure and should be encoded as profile-specific exceptions

toolkit_control: Accept Blocks locks final CSVs; Edit reopens; hosted mode can download generated CSVs
study_examples: Reproducibility and audit trails in BRM-style software papers
design_rationale: Explicit acceptance turns randomization from transient UI state into a citable artifact
caveat: Hosted/static downloads cannot launch local timing without the companion backend

toolkit_control: Participant-by-part block-order manifest
study_examples: Counterbalanced behavioral experiment workflows
design_rationale: Participant count affects block-order permutations and package generation; it should be captured before runner handoff
caveat: The toolkit does not determine statistical power; labs still need study-level power/planning

toolkit_control: Single or pre/post split packages with part-local manifests
study_examples: Training, intervention, tool-use, walking, or pre/post PPS variants
design_rationale: Splitting makes pre/post or intervention designs reconstructable while preserving part identity in markers and analysis
caveat: Contextual interventions remain metadata unless the toolkit controls their delivery

toolkit_control: Regenerate Sequence and saved experiment_block_order.csv
study_examples: Counterbalancing and participant-level schedule assignment
design_rationale: Separates block contents from participant order, allowing reproducible schedule rotations
caveat: Permutation schemes must be reported, especially when blocks encode direction, source class, or part

toolkit_control: Profile snapshot, bridge manifest, output diary, Data_min/Data_max acquisition layout
study_examples: Open materials and reproducibility expectations in software papers
design_rationale: Separates reusable study design from private/session outputs and makes the acquisition root reconstructable
caveat: Participant data and local generated artifacts are not committed to the public repo

toolkit_control: Save Design and Start Experiment Runner launches PPSExperimentRunner.exe with prepared manifests
study_examples: Behavioral timing software and lab-local runner workflows
design_rationale: Browser GUI stays an orchestrator while the native app owns synchronized playback, response logging, LSL, and local outputs
caveat: The runner's software events must be validated separately from hardware loopback and tactile perception

gui_decision: Focus Mode: output levels and test audio/tactile
toolkit_control: Output 1/2 headphone gain, Output 3/4 tactile gain, Test Audio, Test Tactile
study_examples: Lab hardware setup and comfort checks
design_rationale: Operator-facing checks reduce routing mistakes before participant timing begins
caveat: Output-level checks are not calibrated SPL or mechanical-vibration measurements

toolkit_control: two_down_one_up_detection_threshold.v2 over 0.01-0.5 percent Output 3/4 with catch and confirmation phases
study_examples: Vibrotactile threshold, adaptation, recovery, and staircase-method literature
design_rationale: Individual tactile thresholds vary and threshold procedures affect estimates; calibration makes the tactile preset explicit
caveat: Calibration can increase missed trials if the chosen level is near threshold, especially during long tasks; quantify only with traceable artifacts

gui_decision: Focus Mode: adaptive tactile threshold safeguard
toolkit_control: After two tactile misses, raise Output 3/4 by +0.01 percent up to 0.5 percent; log tactile_threshold_adapted and CSV/JSON outputs
study_examples: Vibrotactile adaptation and threshold-shift literature
design_rationale: A narrow operator safeguard acknowledges that detection can drift during long sessions
caveat: This is not yet a validated psychophysical correction and must be analyzed as run-local evidence

toolkit_control: Optional part-end top-up block for missed tactile trials
study_examples: Long audio-tactile tasks with expected occasional misses
design_rationale: Preserves planned tactile exposure and operator transparency when misses occur
caveat: Top-up rows are rescue/quality-control evidence and should be marked separately in analysis

gui_decision: Focus Mode: LSL, LabRecorder, event mirrors, and loopback
toolkit_control: PPSMarkersV2, PPSTriggerCodes, event CSV, XDF capture, audio evidence WAV, optional wired loopback
study_examples: Timing-validation standards in behavioral software and smartphone RT validation
design_rationale: Separates software schedule, recorded marker persistence, digital output evidence, and electrical loopback evidence
caveat: Electrical loopback does not measure Woojer mechanical onset or subjective tactile perception

toolkit_control: Hits, misses, catch correct no-responses, false alarms, top-up markers
study_examples: Reaction-time PPS studies and response-probability critique
design_rationale: Response integrity is shown before model interpretation because hit/catch rates constrain RT inference
caveat: The response panel is operator feedback, not a participant-level scientific conclusion

toolkit_control: condition_mean_pooled_soa baseline correction when baseline rows exist; fall back to raw mean RT
study_examples: Tactile-only and fixed-distance baseline correction designs
design_rationale: Makes baseline subtraction explicit and stores baseline_n and source SOAs
caveat: Pooling baseline SOAs is a pragmatic default and may not match every original paper's correction

toolkit_control: Sigmoid, logarithmic-decay, and linear fits with AICc/Delta AICc triage
study_examples: Canzoneri sigmoid boundary, Hobeika logarithmic/linear distance argument, Holmes critique
design_rationale: Multiple model families prevent a single PPS boundary metaphor from being hard-coded into the software
caveat: Instant analysis is exploratory; confirmatory models require preregistration and adequate cell counts

toolkit_control: Minimal 17-column public CSV plus reconstructive private/session mirror
study_examples: Open-science data minimization and reproducibility practice
design_rationale: Provides a publication-ready table while retaining private reconstruction artifacts outside the public package
caveat: Labs must review ethics/consent before public sharing; local names and raw outputs stay excluded
profile_template_ids: all completed native or phone-owned runs
